reviews.title: A Brilliantly Challenging Spy Puzzle
reviews.body: Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.his was such a clever and absorbing puzzle book. Find the Spy feels much more like working through a real investigation file than simply completing a collection of brain teasers.The 180 suspects initially looked slightly daunting, but that is part of what makes the challenge so satisfying. You genuinely have to pay attention to the details, decode the clues and eliminate suspects methodically rather than relying on guesses. I especially enjoyed the variety of puzzles, with Morse code, ciphers, symbols and logic challenges keeping the investigation interesting throughout.It is challenging without feeling unfair, and the step-by-step solutions are there if you genuinely get stuck without immediately spoiling the whole experience.If you enjoy escape rooms, detective mysteries, code-breaking or logic puzzles, this is an excellent choice. It is the sort of book you can easily lose an evening to because you keep telling yourself you will solve just one more clue.Very clever, genuinely challenging and extremely satisfying when the pieces finally start falling into place. Definitely recommended for puzzle lovers.Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Good Not Great, Very Repetitive
reviews.body: Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.So I am giving this one 3 stars as it's just okay and not what I was hoping for. It's not *bad* by any means but it stops being engaging after just the first few puzzles. The answers to everything start becoming so repetitive that you can easily guess the answer to any given puzzle by solving just the first letter of a code and sometimes just by the word length. I won't spoil it obviously but there are so many agents in the book that it was frustrating to have so many of the answers to puzzles match. I've downloaded the free content to see if it adds anything to the experience but the book itself just doesn't scratch the puzzle itch the way I'd hoped.Read moreRead less
